newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - Cash flows, new junk higher.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - Cash flows, new junk higher.

text.p: Another week of positive inflows to high-yield mutual funds helped power gains for another active day of junk bond issues, while bonds in the secondary market kept pace with Treasuries, dealers said on Friday.

Meanwhile, close to $6 billion in investment grade issues priced this week failed to shake secondary spreads more than a few basis points, traders said. Most new issues held issued bids or tightened when freed to trade, they added.

The U.S. Treasury rallied on Friday following a lower-than-expected Producer Price Index report, underpinning already heady sentiments in high-yield bonds. Issuers were able to upsize offerings and realize gains upon the removal of syndicate restrictions. Still, some new issues expected to price during the week, including national internet service provider Verio Inc's $150 million seven-year senior note, were put off a week as underwriters continued to take orders, said one source close to the deal.

Reflecting strength, Riddell Sports Inc's $115 million 10-1/2 percent par 10-year B2/single-B senior note issue was upsized from $100 million and priced through talk of 10-5/8 percent bandied about earlier.
Riddell notes were seen bid at 102-7/8 at mid-afternoon.
NationsBanc Capital Markets Inc was lead manager.

Other issues priced included Pacalta Resources Ltd's $120 million 10-3/4 percent B2/B-minus seven year debt via Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette and Di Giorgio Corp's $155 million 144A 10 percent 10-year B3/single-B senior notes from Merrill Lynch & Co Inc. Both deals were increased in size.

Market players have pointed to inflows as the primary engine behind recent price gains, especially for dozens of new issues, in the past several weeks. The cash influx, including $627.6 million in the latest reporting week, has amounted to more than $4 billion since the market's short-lived correction in mid-March and early April.
The cash flows are reported weekly by AMG Data Services.

At least a dozen new high-yield issues are expected next week, including the Verio Inc deal and $115 million in debt from North Atlantic Trading Co Inc. North Atlantic will be acquired by smokeless tobacco cigarette rolling paper purveyor National Tobacco Co LP, forming a new company, North American Trading Co.
Big investment grade issues set to come next week include Bayerische Landesbank's $1.0 billion 10-year global offering, according to syndicate officials.
